summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of NRI tax obligations in India, including residential status, taxable income, and benefits of filing ITR. However, some specific numerical claims regarding tax exemption limits and the application of certain rules need clarification or correction based on the latest tax regimes.

claims.claim: An individual is considered a 'Resident' in India for a financial year if they satisfy either of the following basic conditions: 1. They are in India for a period of 182 days or more during the financial year. 2. They are in India for a period of 60 days or more during the financial year AND 365 days or more during the four preceding financial years.
claims.note: These are the basic conditions for determining residential status as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: However, for Indian citizens or Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) who leave India for employment outside India, or as a crew member of an Indian ship, the 60-day period in the second condition is extended to 182 days.

Similarly, for Indian citizens or PIOs who come to India for a visit, the 60-day period is extended to 120 days if their total income (excluding foreign sources) exceeds ₹15 lakhs during the financial year, or 182 days if their total income is up to ₹15 lakhs.
claims.note: This modification to the 60-day rule for Indian citizens/PIOs visiting India is accurate.

claims.claim: Even if your taxable income in India falls below the basic exemption limit (currently ₹2.5 lakhs for individuals below 60 years), it's often prudent for an NRI to file an Income Tax Return (ITR).
claims.note: The basic exemption limit of ₹2.5 lakhs for individuals below 60 years is applicable under the old tax regime. Under the new tax regime, the basic exemption limit is ₹3 lakhs, or ₹4 lakhs for FY 2026-27.

claims.claim: Interest from Non-Resident External (NRE) accounts and FCNR accounts is tax-exempt in India.
claims.note: Interest earned on NRE and FCNR accounts is indeed tax-exempt in India for NRIs.

claims.claim: TDS on NRO FD (30% for NRIs + surcharge + cess): Banks typically deduct TDS at 30% or as per DTAA.
claims.note: The standard TDS rate on NRO fixed deposit interest for NRIs is 30% plus applicable surcharge and cess. DTAA can reduce this rate.

claims.claim: Yes, NRIs can claim certain deductions under Chapter VI-A of the Income Tax Act, such as Section 80C (for investments in PPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums, etc.), 80D (health insurance), and 80G (donations), provided the investments or expenses are made in India.
claims.note: NRIs are eligible to claim various deductions under Chapter VI-A, including 80C, 80D, and 80G, for investments and expenses made in India.

article_title: NRI Tax Filing: When to File ITR After Moving Abroad
